Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Right knee buckling. Osteoarthritis. ACL sprain. Medial meniscus tear. 
Comparison: [REDACTED]. 

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar and multisequence MRI of the right  knee without IV contrast.   

FINDINGS: 

JOINT EFFUSION:  Small joint effusion. Small leaking popliteal cyst. 

ANTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT:  Intact. 

POSTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT:  Intact. 

MEDIAL MENISCUS: Large horizontal undersurface tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is also low-grade tearing of the posterior root attachment. Mild peripheral meniscal extrusion. 

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:  Subchondral fracture line is noted along the weightbearing segment of the medial femoral condyle, with probable nondisplaced osteochondral lesion. This measures 15 mm AP and 10 mm transverse. Moderate degree of associated bone marrow edema.

There is also mild medial compartment osteoarthritis, with subchondral cystic changes of the tibial plateau. 

LATERAL MENISCUS:  Intact.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:  Within normal limits. 

MEDIAL COLLATERAL LIGAMENT:  Edema along the medial collateral ligament suggestive of grade 1 sprain pattern. No discrete tear. 

LATERAL COLLATERAL LIGAMENT COMPLEX:  Intact.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT: Low-grade fissuring of the patellar cartilage. No high-grade or full-thickness cartilage defect. No subchondral edema. 

EXTENSOR APPARATUS:  Superior and inferior patellar enthesophytes. Small interstitial tear in the proximal patellar tendon. 

BONE MARROW:  As above. 
 
OTHER:  None. 


IMPRESSION:

1. Large horizontal undersurface tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Mild peripheral meniscal extrusion.

2. Subchondral fracture line of the medial femoral condyle, likely in the context of nondisplaced osteochondral lesion.

3. Mild medial compartment osteoarthritis.

4. Grade 1 sprain pattern of the medial collateral ligament. Intact cruciate ligaments.

5. Small knee joint effusion and leaking popliteal cyst.
